p01.why: The same conversion function is declared two times in the class.

p02.why: A cast to void never uses the conversion to void, so used stays 0.

p03.why: A conversion function cannot have parameters.

p04.why: take(Target) beats the ellipsis, and its conversion from Source is ambiguous between the constructor and the conversion function.

p05.why: A call by name still calls the conversion to void.

p06.why: The conversion function is defined outside the class and returns 9.

p07.why: D inherits B's conversion to int.

p08.why: A type alias for int names the same target, so D's function hides B's.

p09.why: The operands of built-in + and * convert to int.

p10.why: take(double, int) wins on the second argument, and its first argument needs an ambiguous conversion from Source to double.

p11.why: The switch condition converts to 2 through the one integral conversion.

p12.why: static_assert converts contextually to bool, so the explicit function is usable.

p13.why: take(double) beats the ellipsis, and the conversion from Source to double is ambiguous.

p14.why: A switch condition cannot pick between conversions to int and long.

p15.why: int to D needs two converting constructors.

p16.why: GCC 16 rejects operator auto under -pedantic-errors; GCC 14, Clang, and EDG accept it and the run exits 0 (Q-0059).

p17.why: A conversion function cannot convert to an array type.

p19.why: A standard conversion follows the conversion to int.

p20.why: The noexcept operand converts contextually to bool.

p21.why: A conversion function cannot be a non-member.

p22.why: A non-const conversion function cannot convert a const object.

p23.why: Each initialization picks the function whose target matches exactly.

p24.why: A call by name is valid.

p25.why: The virtual conversion function dispatches to D's, which returns 2.

p26.why: The operand of delete converts to int*.

p27.why: explicit(false) allows the implicit use, and explicit(true) is used only by direct initialization.

p28.why: A to B needs a conversion function and then a converting constructor.

p29.why: A pointer to a function as target needs a type alias.

p30.why: A conversion function cannot convert to a function type.

p31.why: Ref-qualifiers pick & for the lvalue and && for the prvalue.

p32.why: A conversion to its own class draws a default warning, and -Werror turns it into an error.

p33.why: A conversion to a base draws a default warning, and -Werror turns it into an error.

p34.why: A function argument cannot use an explicit conversion function.

p35.why: A conversion function can have an explicit object parameter.

p36.why: The return statement converts S to int.

p37.why: A conversion to void draws a default warning, and -Werror turns it into an error.

p38.why: D's conversion to int hides B's.

p39.why: Parenthesized initialization, static_cast, and int(e) are direct initialization.

p40.why: int to double and long to double rank the same, so the conversion is ambiguous.

p41.why: The operand of built-in == cannot use an explicit conversion function.

p42.why: A conversion function cannot be static.

p43.why: Copy initialization uses the conversion to int.

p44.why: s() calls through the conversion to a function pointer.

p45.why: The conversion to int& returns an lvalue for the member.

p46.why: A constexpr conversion function works in static_assert and in an array bound.

p47.why: The conversion to a base is never used, so the copy constructor slices and used stays 0.

p48.why: The conversion function and the constructor both bind the A prvalue to const A&, so neither is better.

p49.why: The Cell dies at the end of the declaration, before mark(2), and r is never read, so trace is 12.

p50.why: A return statement is copy initialization, so the explicit conversion to bool cannot be used.

p51.why: The operand of built-in + cannot use an explicit conversion function.

p52.why: An array bound in new cannot pick between conversions to int and long.

p53.why: Copy initialization cannot use the explicit conversion to bool.

p54.why: Copy initialization cannot use the explicit conversion to int.

p55.why: Every use is a contextual conversion to bool.

p56.why: A conversion function cannot have a return type before operator.

p57.why: The conversion to its own class is never used, so used stays 0.

p58.why: s() calls through the conversion to a function reference.

p60.why: A condition can use an explicit conversion only when its target is bool.

p61.why: int x{S{}} is direct initialization, so the explicit function is usable.

p62.why: The new array bound converts to 3.

p63.why: The conversion to double does not hide the base's conversion to int, so both give 1.

p64.why: The conversion to int* points at the member.
